title: Dizzy Kaomoji (@_@): Copy & Paste Spiral Eye Text Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste dizzy kaomoji: spiral eyes like (@_@) and (◎_◎;), swirl faces ( ꩜ ᯅ ꩜;), knocked-out (×_×) and seeing-stars faces like ☆⌒(>。<).
hero_tagline: Spiral eyes, swirling heads and knocked-out faces for when the room will not stop spinning. Click a face to put it on your clipboard.
intro: Cartoons show dizziness with spiral eyes, and the @ sign is the closest spiral on a keyboard, so (@_@) has meant dizzy, dazed or overwhelmed for decades. It covers spinning after a ride, too much homework, a confusing explanation or a long day. ◎ makes a rounder, ringed eye, and ꩜, a Cham punctuation mark shaped like a true spiral, is the newer aesthetic version. X eyes are a different state: (×_×) means knocked out or finished, the face after the dizziness wins. Stars ☆ around the head show a bump, the way cartoon characters see stars after hitting something.

sections.label: Spiral @ Eyes
sections.intro: The @ face works almost everywhere because @ is on every keyboard and in every font.

sections.label: Swirl Eyes
sections.intro: ◎ draws a ringed eye and ꩜ a full spiral. ꩜ comes from the Cham script, so some older devices show a box instead.

sections.label: Knocked Out
sections.intro: X eyes for when the dizziness has won. Also used jokingly for "I'm done" after a long task.

sections.label: Seeing Stars
sections.intro: ☆ and ⌒ show something flying into the head, the cartoon cue for a bonk.

sections.label: Wobbling
sections.intro: Arms and tildes add movement, for walking off a roller coaster or standing up too fast.

faq.a: It means dizzy, dazed or overwhelmed. The @ signs stand in for the spiral eyes cartoons draw on a character whose head is spinning, and people use it for anything from motion sickness to information overload.

faq.q: What is the difference between (@_@) and (×_×)?
faq.a: (@_@) is still conscious, just spinning or confused. (×_×) uses cartoon X eyes for knocked out or finished, so it reads as the stage after the dizziness.

faq.q: Why does ꩜ show as a box?
faq.a: ꩜ is a punctuation mark from the Cham script of Vietnam and Cambodia, and some older phones and computers have no font for it. The @ and ◎ faces use common characters and display on nearly every device.
